metadata.title: Tokenmaxxing is out, but companies are still spending on AI. What's changed?

content.text:
In just a short amount of time, corporate policy on "tokenmaxxing" — or excessively using AI models to inflate usage on internal leaderboards — has already peaked and valleyed. After seeing their bill for AI tokens, many companies have shifted toward a more efficient outlook on AI spending.
Tabs CEO Ali Hussain discusses what's changed within corporate AI pricing and what this pivot may mean for OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) and Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) ahead of their mega-IPOs.
Token maxing, the practice of maximizing AI token usage was Silicon Valley's latest trend until companies got the bill.
Sticker shock from ballooning AI costs now have many corporations rethinking AI spending and how artificial intelligence is being implemented.
Our next guest says this means companies will change how they spend on AI. Joining us for more is Ali Hussein, the CEO of Tabs.
Tabs is an AI revenue platform that automates billing and collections for finance teams. It also recently raised $55 million in its series B funding round.
Ali, thank you so much for being with us. I I just want to first set the scene here. Walk us through the white space opportunity that you saw within this market.
Absolutely. So thank you so much for having me. Um, overall, I mean, AI is going to fundamentally change pricing as we know it.
And when we looked back when we founded the company two and a half years ago, um we saw that pricing was already starting to shift. People were moving from flat fee or more predictable pricing models to contracts that opened the door for a lot more usage and variability.
We really think we're in the first stage of this. Early days have been, let's try to get some form of um, pass through of the tokens or the actual cost of this AI compute.
But as we're starting to see the scale, it's honestly getting complicated. Most companies are starting to just themselves get comfortable with what the cost of these tokens are and as they're changing commercially, this is just changing the way business to business is thinking about it.
And so, that was really the catalyst, this level of uncertainty to start to think about how we're going to rethink accounting infrastructure to support this and has been an amazing journey so far as Tabs has been able to support some of the fastest growing companies in the world like Cursur and, um, OAC security and many others.
Yeah, Cursur, a company that just got acquired by SpaceX, definitely one to watch there.
But you also some of our viewers might be familiar with what happened over at at Uber where they were offering tokens to their to their employees and then they actually had to cut back because of the cost.
So what sort of ripple effect does this have on other big tech companies? I mean, like a Microsoft, and Amazon, a Google, who are all looking to to be more efficient now knowing that this is the case.
I think there's a few things. I mean I talk to CFOs every day. I think there's a few that have their processes now getting readjusted the learnings the last six months and they just feel more certainty.
So for them, it's more about stay the course. They've just been able to budget and plan for it, I think much longer than what we may have seen in the Uber case.
I think there's a handful of others, um, especially at the large corporate level, which have huge costs. They're just trying to get control of the situa- situation.
I don't yet believe there's going to be massive pullback in token admin, but I think a lot of these CFOs are now finding ways to uh find a lot more certainty.
And so what we're seeing is a lot of these companies are just procuring directly from the research labs the level of compute they need at the best cost and are just planning for this on a quarterly basis versus thinking they can plan out a full year.
And on the reverse case here, when you think about a company like Open AI or Anthropic, they're also now competing to make sure that these companies maintain their spend with them. So, what would be your message to to those companies on that end of the spectrum here?
I think one is you just got to up the tooling that allows a lot more transparency to your buyer. And we hear this all the time where a CFO wakes up the next morning and an engineer utilized half a million dollars of tokens.
And I think guard rails are going to matter and just really good transparency that allows the planning. But I don't yet believe it's going to fundamentally shift any type of pricing right now as as we know a lot of the research labs are looking to go public in the next six to nine months.
And so I still think they're going to be looking for optimal pricing and value especially given the mass scale and control they have right now with just two or three options in the market.
But I think tooling that gives more visibility and controls to the customer will certainly be the next step.
And it almost seems like we're still in the early innings of adoption because sure, we're hearing about these big tech players, but it seems like maybe mid-sized companies haven't even fully adopted this just yet, but at the same time, we're hearing that California now is giving their agencies access to Claude.
What did you make of that announcement and and what does that mean maybe for this overall model within the government system moving forward?
I think it's inevitable. I think obviously tech forward companies were the first to adopt.
I spend about 50% of my time with providers like you mentioned, nonprofits, government, um, a lot of professional services. They're now in the early innings.
I think what's going to be interesting and this is what we see on the tab side is a lot of them are not going to be directly procurring procuring the AI from Anthropic or Open AI. It's going to come from vertical solutions that embed the tokens within.
And so, I think for them it's going to be getting really smart on how they're procuring their contract with Salesforce or with their ERP, etc., that is going to start to give them access to tokens, which is going to have to allow them to really rethink pricing and how they pay for things with a lot more variability than they've had in the past.
Ali, such great insight. Thank you so much. I appreciate your time as we scope out how these early innings eventually play out.
Thank you so much.
Of course. Thanks for having me. Take care.
